Implementation Plan Planning ref: `main` at `0b14e3db33a62775f84c83a8f85ddb6998bc2738` (symbolic branch `main`). The integration branch metadata is also `main`, so there is no mismatch. Answers used: - **Q1 = A:** make the host-only refusal diagnosable without changing what gets merged. - **Q2 = A:** run the diagnostics at both `check-paths` call sites. One correction to how Q2 was framed. The two call sites are not "pre-review" versus "after the editor": - `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:2289` runs in every resolver mode, including `AUTOFIX_PRE_REVIEW_RESOLVE=true`. - `:2513` is the re-check on the Claude-engine branch. Both call sites send rejections through `_resolver_fail_closed_for_conflict_paths` (`:595-607`). Adding the diagnostics there covers both with no extra calls. Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends `_resolver_fail_closed_for_conflict_paths` (`scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`) Scope-mode justification: The approved option is diagnostics only. The host-only refusal, the `sandbox_path_host_only` reason, the `::error::` headline, `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON` and the retry-state persistence all stay exactly as they are. The only runtime change is a set of extra stderr lines, emitted on the host-only branch just before the existing fail-closed exit, saying why each host-only path is in the conflict set. The rest of this paragraph explains which parts of the issue's fix constraints this meets. Part of the "remove the cause" constraint is already met. The retry loop that kept failing is already stopped: `conflict_resolver_sandbox_path_host_only` is listed in `NON_RETRYABLE_FAILURE_REASONS`, so the identical-failure cap trips on the first failure marker. What was still missing is the evidence a human needs to merge PR #6549, and that the heal intake needs before it can classify the failure. That evidence is the hook's index stages, its blob ids on each side, whether the template copy is also conflicted, whether each side's live and template copies match, and which source put the path in `conflicted_paths.txt`. The complete version (summary line, per-path stage and blob data, template parity, source classification, plus the test-harness and docs updates) adds roughly 60 lines of shell over a bare stage dump. It adds no new dependency or interface. Under the Boil the Lake rule (§6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the complete version wins. ## 1. Files likely to change files_touched: - `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` - `tests/test_review_conflict_resolve_sandbox_only.py` - `tests/test_review_sandbox_claude_roles.py` - `agents.md` - `changelog.d/6764-host-only-conflict-diagnostics.md` (new) No workflow YAML changes, so the §24 size limit is not affected. `review_conflict_resolve.sh` is already a staged runtime helper, so no `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS` change is needed. Nothing under `.claude/` or `workflow-templates/` changes. ## 2. Functions / modules **`scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`** 1. New function `_resolver_report_host_only_conflict_details()`. I searched the repo for this name and for the `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_HOST_ONLY_DIAG` prefix and found no matches. - Place it immediately before `_resolver_fail_closed_for_conflict_paths()`. - Argument `$1` is the check-paths report file. It reads only lines matching the regex the caller already validated, `^host_only\t[A-Za-z0-9_.][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*$`, and processes at most 20 paths, the same cap as the `::error::` line. - Emit one summary line, using only local git reads (index, refs, trees; no blob content, no GitHub API): `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_HOST_ONLY_DIAG merge_head= merge_base= host_only_paths=` - `merge_head` comes from `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD`. - `merge_base` comes from `git merge-base HEAD MERGE_HEAD`, only when `merge_head` is set. - Emit one line per path: `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_HOST_ONLY_DIAG path=

source= stages=<1,2,3|none> stage1= stage2= stage3= head_blob= merge_head_blob=<...> base_blob=<...> template= template_unmerged= template_head_blob=<...> template_merge_head_blob=<...> template_base_blob=<...> live_eq_template_head= live_eq_template_merge_head=<...> live_eq_template_base=<...>` - How each field is filled: - **Stages and their oids:** `git ls-files --unmerged -- "

"`, which reads the index only. - **`source`:** `unmerged` if any index stage exists. Otherwise `marker` if `git grep -lE '^(<<<<<<< |>>>>>>> )' -- "

"` matches, using the same regex as `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh:975`. Otherwise `other` (fingerprint expansion or something not identified). - **Blob ids at each revision:** `git rev-parse -q --verify ":

"`. This is a tree lookup, so it fetches no blobs in the blobless review checkout. Output is `absent` when the path does not exist at that revision, and `unknown` when the revision is unavailable. - **Template mapping:** only for paths beginning `.claude/`, where the template is `workflow-templates/

`; otherwise `template=none` and the `template_*` and `live_eq_*` fields are `unknown`. - **`live_eq_template_*`:** a comparison of blob oids at the same revision. It is `unknown` when either side is absent or unavailable. - Every oid is checked against `^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$` before printing; anything else prints as `unknown`. - The function is fail-open. Each git call uses `2>/dev/null || true`, the whole body runs in a subshell, and it always returns 0, even outside a git repo (every field then reads `unknown`/`none`). 2. Edit `_resolver_fail_closed_for_conflict_paths()`. Inside the existing `if [ -n "${conflict_host_only_paths}" ]` branch, the order becomes: 1. The unchanged `::error::Conflict resolver: host-only conflicted path(s) need a manual merge: ...` line. 2. The new call `_resolver_report_host_only_conflict_details "${conflict_path_report}" >&2 || true`. 3. The unchanged `_resolver_fail_closed sandbox_path_host_only`. The `unsafe` / `sandbox_path_unsupported` branch is untouched and still prints no names. ## 3. Data structures affected - No state, schema, comment-marker or env-var changes. - `resolver_conflict_path_report.txt` is read but its format does not change. - The new stderr lines reach the failure evidence through the existing stage-stderr capture (`resolver_stage_stderr.txt` and `failure_evidence_tail.txt`), so the heal intake and humans see them without new wiring. ## 4. API / interface changes - Adds the stable log prefix `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_HOST_ONLY_DIAG`. It is registered in `agents.md` in both the "Stable log prefixes" list and the `LOG_PREFIX.name=` block. - No new env vars or flags. The function runs only on a path that already ends the run. ## Decisions ### D1 — Diagnostics only, keep the fail-closed exit - Chosen: add a per-path merge-provenance report on the host-only branch; leave the refusal and every reason/marker unchanged. - Alternatives considered: copying the template over the live hook, with or without a parity guard (rejected in the earlier round: either it never fires, or it lets unreviewed template content into a hook that runs on the host); no code change (does not meet the issue's requirement for a reproducing regression test). - Why: approved Q1 = A. It improves operational clarity without touching the security boundary (§6), and it is the evidence the heal diagnosis said was missing. ### D2 — Plain prefixed stderr lines, not `::error::`/`::warning::` - Chosen: plain lines with a `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_HOST_ONLY_DIAG` prefix, avoiding the words `error`, `fatal` and `FAILED`. - Alternatives considered: `::warning::` annotations; more `::error::` lines. - Why: - `workflow_failure_heal.py` takes the failure headline from the first specific `::error::` line, and computes `error_signature` from `::error::` lines before any fallback pattern (`_SIGNATURE_PATTERNS`, `:253-258`). - Plain lines therefore leave the headline, the heal fingerprint and lineage dedup unchanged (pinned by `test_host_only_error_is_the_failure_headline`). - Annotations would add noise to every run. ### D3 — Separate helper function, with the test harness extracting it - Chosen: a new top-level function, plus a matching extractor in the test harness. - Alternatives considered: inlining the loop in `_resolver_fail_closed_for_conflict_paths`; calling it behind a `type ... >/dev/null &&` guard. - Why: it keeps the fail-closed helper short and readable. A guarded call could silently drop diagnostics if the function went missing, while an unguarded call plus a contract test catches that. ### D4 — Both call sites through the shared helper - Chosen: one change in `_resolver_fail_closed_for_conflict_paths`. - Alternatives considered: adding diagnostics only at `:2289`. - Why: approved Q2 = A. One code path costs nothing extra. ## Security considerations - **Trust boundary is unchanged.** The live hook stays excluded (`scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:120-122`). No model runs, and nothing is written to the worktree or index. Every git command used is read-only (`ls-files`, `rev-parse`, `merge-base`, `grep`). - **Injection into logs and workflow commands.** Path names in the conflict set come from PR content. - The helper only handles paths that already passed the caller's strict `host_only` regex (letters, digits, `._/-`), so a path cannot carry `::`-style workflow commands or a newline. - Oids are regex-checked before printing. - Each path is passed to git after `--`, so it cannot be read as an option. - **No secrets.** The diagnostics print blob/commit oids and repo paths only, never file content, remote URLs or tokens.
